newsitem.title: USA: COMPETITORS MAY LIMIT STARBUCKS PRICE HIKE.
newsitem.headline: COMPETITORS MAY LIMIT STARBUCKS PRICE HIKE.

text.p: Starbucks Corp said on Wednesday its any decision to raise prices may be curtailed by competitors who choose not to raise prices.

In a quarterly regulatory filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Starbucks said its ability to raise prices further in response to rising coffee prices may be limited by competitive pressures if other major speciality coffee retailers do not also raise prices.
At the end of May, Starbucks raised its prices for the second time this year to reflect sharply higher world coffee prices.
If coffee prices remain at their current levels, Starbucks said it will continue to incur substantially higher costs for the speciality coffee it purchases.
Also, the Seattle based-chain, said rapid sharp decreases in the cost of green coffee could also pressure it to lower sales prices before realizing cost reductions in its green coffee inventory.
Starbucks' inability to pass through higher coffee prices in the form of higher retail prices for beans and beverages could have a material adverse effect on earnings, it said.
The company said it entered into fixed price purchase commitments in order to secure an adequate supply of quality green coffee and establish firm prices for future periods.

As of June 29, Starbucks had about $43 million in fixed price purchase commitments which, together with existing inventory, should provide an adequate supply of green coffee for the balance of fiscal 1997 and well into fiscal 1998.

In addition to fluctating coffee prices, Starbuck's future results of operations and earnings could be significantly impacted by factors such as increased competition within the speciality coffee industry.

Starbucks also cited its ability to find optimal store locations at reasonable lease rates, increased costs associated with opening and operating retail stores in new markets and ability to obtain adequate capital to finance its planned expansion.
